useWhen: Use CONSUMABLE when the source is used up or carried as a stack: a potion, elixir or oil, a spell scroll, ammunition, poison, food and drink, gear with a number of uses (a healer's kit), or a one-use wondrous item such as dust or a bead. The parser also accepts `wand` and `rod` here, for a charged wand or rod that the user wants stored as a consumable.
smallest: `ITEM.Name` (the name), `ITEM.Consumable Type` (`ammo`, `food`, `poison`, `potion`, `rod`, `scroll`, `trinket` or `wand`). `ammo` also needs `AMMUNITION_PROPERTIES.Ammunition Type`; `poison` also needs `POISON_PROPERTIES.Poison Type`.
notFor: The bow, crossbow or sling that fires the ammunition: WEAPON.
A spell description that is not a scroll: SPELL.
A ring, cloak, boots or other permanent magic item: EQUIPMENT. A wand or rod fits either template; EQUIPMENT (`Equipment Type: wand` or `rod`) suits one that keeps recharging.
A quiver, bag or case that holds the consumables: CONTAINER.
A herbalism kit, poisoner's kit or other kit that gives a tool proficiency: TOOL.
A gem, an art object, or gear that is not used up: LOOT.

checks: `ITEM.Consumable Type` is one of `ammo`, `food`, `poison`, `potion`, `rod`, `scroll`, `trinket`, `wand`, `wondrous`. `ammunition` fails. Elixirs, oils and philters are `potion`. Use `wondrous` for a wondrous item that is used up, and `trinket` for a consumable that fits no other type.

`ammo` needs `AMMUNITION_PROPERTIES.Ammunition Type` and `poison` needs `POISON_PROPERTIES.Poison Type`, or the import fails. Leave `ITEM.Consumable Subtype` out: the importer fills it from those two keys. If you do write it, use the matching dnd5e id (`crossbowBolt` for `bolt`), because a value that disagrees is stored without a warning.
Ammunition type words here are `arrow`, `bolt`, `needle`, `bullet`, `slingbullet` and `energycell`. They differ from the ids in the Weapon template.

A one-use item (potion, scroll, dose of poison) is `USAGE.Uses Max: 1`, `USAGE.Uses Spent: 0`, `USAGE.Destroy on Empty: true`. Write `Destroy on Empty` with a lowercase `on`; `Destroy On Empty` is ignored with a warning.
`INVENTORY.Quantity` is how many of the item there are. Do not put the stack size in `USAGE.Uses Max`. Ammunition has no `USAGE`: twenty arrows are `Quantity: 20`.
A +1 on ammunition is `ATTUNEMENT.Magic Bonus: 1` with `PROPERTIES.Magical: true`. Do not use the old `AMMUNITION_PROPERTIES.Magic Bonus` key.
`DAMAGE` is for ammunition that deals its own damage. Do not put a potion's healing or a poison's damage there.

Scroll components are `SCROLL_PROPERTIES.Vocal` (V), `Somatic` (S), `Concentration` and `Ritual`; `Verbal` gives a warning. `FOOD_PROPERTIES` belongs only to `Consumable Type: food`; on another type it gives a warning. Always write `ITEM.Rarities` (`[]` for mundane arrows, food or poison; a missing key is stored as `common`) and `INVENTORY.Identified` (a missing key follows the user's setting).
